candidates.title: Frame monetization options for a freemium app

demandEvidence.chore: Seeking conceptual help with monetization for a freemium app.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: looking for some conceptual help with one of my freemium apps.

experimentPlan.output: A one-page set of monetization options with assumptions and questions for the app owner to review.
experimentPlan.trigger: The app owner supplies a short description and asks for options.
steps: Record the supplied app purpose and user group.
List possible value exchanges as hypotheses.
Compare options against the supplied constraints.
Draft questions that would test user interest.
Have the app owner review every assumption.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fictional app brief, confirm every option traces to an input and each uncertain market claim is labeled as a question or hypothesis.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The owner supplies accurate product details, chooses research participants, and makes all pricing and product decisions.
unverified: No app category, users, current conversion data, or constraints are retained in the supplied spans.
No source supports market sizing, pricing advice accuracy, or customer acquisition.

ease.reason: A fictional brief can be organized by a beginner, but source detail and any supporting monetization capability are absent.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: indie app developers might pay for structured monetization advice; this request establishes no payment or buyer scope.

feasibility.reason: A worksheet can be tested in four weeks, but the post gives no app details or way to validate advice.

autonomy.reason: The proposed options draft is repeatable, but an owner must supply context and make every commercial decision.

evidence.reason: The post asks for conceptual help with a freemium app but supplies no app category, monetization task, or constraints.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the assigned discussion and scoped proposal; provisional mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

candidates.title: Draft shipment delay alerts from supplied rows

demandEvidence.chore: Notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed, copy an order update into a CRM, alert a buyer when inventory drops, or send a daily report to a team channel.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed shipment exception sheet listing supplied delayed orders and a draft dispatcher alert for each.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes a test shipment table into a local prototype.
steps: Validate required fields in the supplied rows.
Apply an operator-defined delay rule.
Create one draft alert per flagged row.
Mark incomplete or conflicting rows for review.
Ask a dispatcher to verify and approve any message.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Using fictional rows with known statuses, verify every flagged row meets the stated delay rule and every draft preserves its supplied order identifier.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A dispatcher supplies and verifies status data, defines the delay rule, and approves any communication; no carrier connection or sending is proposed.
unverified: Actual shipment fields and delay thresholds are not specified.
Live order feeds and message delivery are not documented.

ease.reason: Fictional rows make a small alert draft approachable, but no attached reference supports logistics intake or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: ecommerce operators may value reviewed shipment alerts; the discussion does not establish purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week offline row-to-alert mock is bounded; real shipment feeds and sending are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A rule can flag supplied rows, but a dispatcher must verify status and approve messages; no integration is documented.

evidence.reason: A retained task span lists shipment delay notifications among examples, without fields, recurrence, or corroborating demand.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the assigned discussion and scoped proposal; provisional mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

candidates.title: Check weekly keyword metric rows

demandEvidence.chore: Add each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets every week.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Runs VNCNT Labs’ Keyword Search Volume Actor on Apify every week and adds each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets.

experimentPlan.output: A checked weekly keyword table with supplied keyword, volume, CPC, and difficulty columns.
experimentPlan.trigger: The operator provides a weekly keyword list and a sample result table.
steps: Check that each result has a keyword and three metric fields.
Place supplied values into the named columns.
Flag missing or duplicate keyword rows.
Summarize rows needing correction.
Have an SEO operator verify values before use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare output rows against a hand-labeled fictional input table and confirm values stay attached to the correct keyword, with missing fields flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An SEO operator supplies authorized data and verifies its accuracy; the proposed test does not call Apify, persist invoices, or run the source workflow.
unverified: The attached post describes an existing workflow, not an independently verified need from a paying customer.
No supplied reference supports executing the Actor, obtaining live search metrics, or connecting to Sheets.

ease.reason: A beginner can format synthetic metrics, but no attached reference supports running the described Actor or Sheets connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional SEO consultants may pay for recurring keyword reports; this workflow description proves no buyer demand.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can check sample rows, while live metric retrieval and integration remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed table checks repeat, but a person must verify source metrics; no supplied reference supports execution.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly describes a weekly workflow and metric columns, but it is a single workflow description, not corroborated customer demand.

candidates.title: Turn rough sketches into a layout brief

demandEvidence.chore: Translate rough iPad sketches into higher-fidelity wireframes or illustrations.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’ve been looking for a tool that can translate rough sketches on my iPad to higher fidelity wireframes or illustrations in near real time.

experimentPlan.output: A rough layout brief that labels the major elements visible in one supplied sketch for a designer to redraw.
inputs: A designer-supplied list of required elements
experimentPlan.trigger: A designer provides one sketch and requests a draft layout brief.
steps: Record the supplied intended use.
Describe visible regions and labels as uncertain observations.
Map observations to the designer’s requested element list.
Flag ambiguous or unreadable areas.
Return the brief for designer review and redraw.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fictional test sketch with a known element list, verify each listed element is either located in the draft brief or explicitly marked uncertain.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A designer supplies lawful test images, interprets ambiguous marks, checks the brief, and creates or approves final artwork.
unverified: No supplied implementation source supports image interpretation or wireframe generation.
The request does not specify image formats, fidelity criteria, or frequency.

ease.reason: The request describes image conversion, but no attached source supports interpreting sketches or generating wireframes.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent designers might pay to speed sketch conversion; this request establishes no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could test labeled observations, but image interpretation and fidelity are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A draft description could be reviewed, but a designer must interpret ambiguity and produce the final layout.

evidence.reason: The post states a specific sketch-to-wireframe or illustration need, but no frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the assigned discussion and scoped proposal; provisional mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

candidates.title: Prepare game-test CSV rows for review

demandEvidence.chore: Log mobile-game test measurements, export the notes as CSV, and paste them into Google Sheets; the attempted trigger misses or duplicates files.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

experimentPlan.output: A review-ready table from a supplied game-test CSV, with duplicate rows flagged before import.
inputs: Synthetic CSV with frame drops and notes
experimentPlan.trigger: A tester supplies an exported sample CSV for one session.
steps: Extract CSV rows into structured fields.
Check required measurement columns.
Compare rows using the operator-selected key.
Flag repeated or incomplete rows.
Have a tester verify and import the reviewed table.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Run a labeled fictional CSV containing known complete, incomplete, and repeated rows; confirm extracted values match and only expected duplicates are flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A tester chooses the deduplication key, reviews every flagged row, and imports approved data; phone triggers and live Google Sheets writes are outside this proposed test.
unverified: Phone upload timing and trigger behavior remain unresolved.
The right duplicate key and real CSV formats are not supplied.

ease.reason: The n8n CSV extraction docs (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74) and duplicate removal docs (f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108) support row extraction and comparisons, not phone intake.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent game testers may pay for cleaner session-log imports; the post establishes no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic CSV prototype fits documented extraction and duplicate operations in 5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74 and f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108; phone uploads stay unresolved.

autonomy.reason: The docs support extracting rows and removing selected duplicates (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74; f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108), while a tester chooses keys and reviews imports.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe typed game measurements, later CSV export and sheet pasting, and repeated or missed file triggers; this is one post.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the assigned discussion and scoped proposal; provisional mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.
